Two separately written verifiers, TypeScript (npm) and Python (PyPI), run
against the same published vectors with the same pinned key.

> Both implementations produced identical verdicts for every published vector.

## Argument member-name order

`test-vectors/action/args/`, each object as an `anchor-v1` envelope verified with
`--envelope anchor-v1`. Member names sort by UTF-16 code unit (RFC 8785 section
3.2.3). The envelope signed over code-point order must be refused wherever the
two orders differ.

| Vector | Expected | TypeScript | Python | Agree |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `001-non-bmp-vs-fullwidth.json (code unit)` | valid | accept | accept | yes |
| `001-non-bmp-vs-fullwidth.json (code point)` | invalid | reject | reject | yes |
| `002-cjk-extension-b.json (code unit)` | valid | accept | accept | yes |
| `002-cjk-extension-b.json (code point)` | invalid | reject | reject | yes |
| `003-common-prefix.json (code unit)` | valid | accept | accept | yes |
| `003-common-prefix.json (code point)` | invalid | reject | reject | yes |
| `004-nfc-nfd-distinct-names.json (code unit)` | valid | accept | accept | yes |
| `004-nfc-nfd-distinct-names.json (code point)` | valid | accept | accept | yes |
| `005-nested.json (code unit)` | valid | accept | accept | yes |
| `005-nested.json (code point)` | invalid | reject | reject | yes |
| `006-ascii-only.json (code unit)` | valid | accept | accept | yes |
| `006-ascii-only.json (code point)` | valid | accept | accept | yes |

## Reproducing this

```
python3 scripts/conformance-report.py
```

Both verifiers require an explicit `--key`. Neither will verify a receipt
against the public key carried inside that same receipt unless
`--integrity-only` is passed, because a signature checked against a key the
receipt supplies proves only that whoever held that key signed it.
